newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON HOPES TO BURY MEMORIES OF BAD SEASON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON HOPES TO BURY MEMORIES OF BAD SEASON.

text.p: Michael Johnson hopes to bury the memories of a troublesome season by successfully defending his world 400 metres title on Tuesday.
After almost crashing out in an earlier round because of a badly-judged finish, the 200 and 400 metres Olympic champion made his way into the final with a confident victory in Monday's semifinals.
The American, the biggest name at the Athens event, said he was ready for a big night after a season dominated by injury and disappointment.
Johnson began the season badly, suffering a thigh injury in his lucrative 150 metres showdown with Olympic 100 metres champion Donovan Bailey in Toronto at the start of June.
When he returned to the track at the Paris Grand Prix later in the month, he suffered a rare defeat.
He came to Athens without having competed at the top level since the Paris disappointment but overall he has shown composure and good form on his way to the final.
Johnson is likely to face fierce competition from compatriot American Tyree Washington who won the other semifinal on Monday and said he was not afraid of the sport's biggest name.

American high hurdler Allen Johnson, who has often had to stand in the shadow of some of his better-known compatriots, will begin the defence of his world title on the fourth day of the championships.
Olympic champion Johnson, who will try to use the first two round of the 110 metres hurdles to advance to the semifinals, sometimes feels he does not receive the consideration he deserves.

"I just get the impression from a lot of different people that they see me as a great hurdler only because they have to," said Johnson, whose most dangerous rivals should be German Florian Schwarthoff and Cuban Anier Garcia.
In the long jump final world champion Ivan Pedroso will be eager to make up for a disappointing showing at last year's Olympics where he was hampered by a hamstring injury and ended a poor 12th.
Pedroso suggested he would be hard to beat by leaping an impressive year's best of 8.63 metres in June.
